Title: Passage 2: Clues to the Perfect Gift
Author: by Lissa Rovetch
Content: Every Father's Day goes the exact same way in my house. My sister, brother, mom, and I bring my dad breakfast in bed. He always does a good job of acting surprised, even though I doubt he's surprised at all! So this `text(year)` ... I wanted to give him something special. Only I had `text(zero)` idea what that could be.
When I was hanging out at the pool after swim class, I asked my friends for ideas.
“We always get my dad a new baseball cap,” said Lana.
“That'd be perfect,” I said. “But my dad refuses to wear anything other than his ratty old 'lucky' hat.”

“When I was little, I used to check out this `text(one)` book from the library over and over again,” said Isabel... “A girl is trying to find the perfect present for her mom, and a giant rabbit comes along and tells her to think about what her mom really likes...”
“OK, I understand,” I said. “You're saying I should think about my dad's favorite things.”
I didn't happen to know any giant rabbits. But I did know `text(two)` cats who have a history of giving good advice.
“You guys spend a lot of time with Dad,” I said to my cats when I got home.
“What do you think he likes most?”
In reply, my younger kitty, Charlie, hopped onto the table by the big chair in our living room. He landed on a pile of my dad's mystery novels.
“That's it!” I said. “Dad loves to read. Especially mystery novels. But what if I get `text(one)` he's already read? I can't ask which `text(one)` he'd like because then it wouldn't be a surprise.”
Just then, my older cat, Cow, started batting something around. It was a marker from my marker set.
“That's where the green marker went!” I said.
And suddenly, I knew just what to do. I gave Cow an extra-long ear scratch in exchange for my marker, and then I got to work writing my very own mystery.
